covers: the mismatch warnings, the anchor snapshot and the override record are stored and returned
the override actually reached the matching: the same admission without it differs by exactly the overridden amount
a caller-supplied run warning rides along after the detected ones
an unknown run-record key or a non-numeric amount is refused before anything is stored
the earlier store, pairing, permission, per-file diagnostics, batch delete and replay cases
the workbook carries the stored warning text, the manual-entry banner and the trace section
the trace row states the user value and its cell comment states the reader value and the difference
a task with no run record renders neither section

checks.note: the four-language warning table is registered in scripts/i18n/keep-cjk.tsv as intentional, like the workbook label tables

intentional_differences: the deployed run detected the mismatch warnings while orchestrating a run; the native store applies the same rule at admission over the rows it stores and the matched count, in the caller's language

the anchor reader values come from the caller instead of a parser; a missing anchor key falls back to the header amount the caller also sent, and an override may be the replacement amount alone (the stored record still names the reader value)
the three deployed keys live inside the task payload; natively they are one task column whose keys keep the deployed names, read back by the export
a task admitted without anchors stores no snapshot, where the deployed run always wrote one; there is no run orchestration on this side to invent reader values from
the four anchor amounts beside the summary are now stored as columns, which the native bank store had left at zero
